newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower again, origin selling noted.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower again, origin selling noted.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices ended broadly lower for the second straight session as traders once again took profits on the market's recent rally, dealers said.
Brushing aside its opening call, the market headed into negative territory from the outset, where it remained for the rest of the day.

Roaster-linked buying provided support on the dips, as the processing sector took advantage of the lowest prices in a week. The selling was broad-based, but producing countries, who have held back on sales in the hope that prices would go higher still, were strong sellers on Friday, dealers said.
"Once it opened lower, we got a lot of selling from origin," said one broker. "They are afraid that the rally is done."
But traders said the market's recent bull run, in which prices have risen by more than 50 percent to their highest level in nearly two and a half years, appeared far from over, traders said.
"The market could come off to 182-180 cents and still be in an upward trend," the trader said.
Benchmark May futures finished down 3.90 cents at 189.90 cents a lb after trading from 187.50 to 193.50 cents. Spot March, which expires in a 10 days, shed 6.20 to 205.75.
Turnover was estimated at 12,858 lots against Thursday's tally of 15,515 lots.
Traders generally downplayed the effect of today's April options expiry on the futures market, saying options activity had mainly shifted to May and July positions.
In other news, operations returned to normal on Friday at Brazil's port of Paranagua, as dockworkers ended a two-day work stoppage.

Certified coffee stocks grew for the second day in a row, reaching 24,845 60-kg bags as of March 6, CSCE reported after the close of trading. There were an additional 21,869 bags pending grading, the exchange said. ((-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
